grading_system.evidence: Each course taken will have a set of proficiencies associated with the class. Success on those proficiencies will determine if a student will earn credit for the class.
grading_system.proficiency_scale: 1-4 (1 Little to no Evidence; 2 Nearly or partially Meets Standards; 3 Meets Standards; 4 Exceeds Standards)

schedule.evidence: Many Career Center Programs meet ONE BLOCK for one or two semesters, allowing students to retain a full schedule that prepares them for post-secondary success.

credit_definition.text: not_stated as a general rule. Course listings show 1/2 credit for many semester courses (e.g., Social Skills, Printmaking) but 1 credit for some semester-long courses (English 10 Enrichment); full-year English 9 Enrichment = 2 credits.

local_grad_requirements.conversion_note: Credits as stated in the catalog; no conversion needed. Also requires a Senior Project and 40 hours of community service (non-credit). Promotion minimums: 6 credits to grade 10, 13 to grade 11, 20 to grade 12.

flexible_pathways_listed: Vermont Adult Learning High School Completion Program
notes: Graduation (p.2): English 4, Social Studies 3 (incl. 1 U.S. History and 1 modern world studies), Science 3, Math 4 (incl. Algebra I), Fine Arts 1, PE 1.5, Health 1, World Language 1, Electives 9.5; Senior Project required; 40 community service hours non-credit. Grades are both a four-point proficiency scale and traditional letter grades; GPA is weighted by level. Schedule: courses described as 'full block', 'half block', 'semester /Block'; number of blocks per day and whether the day is 4x4 or A/B is not stated, so type is 'other' and courses_per_term is null. Credit per course is not given as one general rule (see credit_definition). Algebra I Part I and Part II are each listed as '2 credits*' (asterisk not explained in the excerpt read). RVTC can give embedded academic credit for some 2-year programs (p.46).
